readerQuestion: How do I set up Home Assistant voice without cloud speech processing, and how do I check which part is failing?
directAnswer: Use Home Assistant OS with Speech-to-Phrase for supported commands and languages, or Whisper for general transcription, plus the built-in Home Assistant agent and Piper. Start through Assist in the phone app or Voice Preview Edition. Standard Voice PE uses on-device microWakeWord, not a mandatory openWakeWord app. Expose one locally controlled lamp and test the dashboard, typed Assist, spoken Assist, and an optional internet-outage repeat in order.
originalContribution: The one-lamp acceptance procedure separates device control, command interpretation, speech recognition, satellite configuration and offline dependencies. The comparison table separates recognition from spoken replies. The troubleshooting sequence directs readers to the failing stage instead of replacing hardware or adjusting microphone gain blindly.
limitations: Documentation research and website rendering tests, not hands-on Home Assistant hardware tests. No measured latency, microphone pickup distance, battery life, price, or installed-device compatibility is claimed. A successful offline check demonstrates that tested route at that time, not a traffic audit or a guarantee about every device. Current firmware, languages, models and exposed entities affect results. The retained illustrative cover is not a Voice PE product photograph or a tested installation. A successful deployment does not establish indexing or ranking recovery.

claimChecks.claim: The guided local stack uses HAOS apps, local recognition, the Home Assistant agent, Piper, and exposed entities.
Voice PE standard firmware uses on-device microWakeWord. Whisper Base guidance specifies at least N100-class hardware, not guaranteed latency.
Voice PE wake-word selection is on its ESPHome device page under Configuration.
Server-side wake detection receives audio before recognition; on-device detection follows a different path.
Wyoming connects local speech services; it is not the protocol for every component in an Assist pipeline.
Speech-to-Phrase is constrained by supported phrases and names. Custom known list values do not make it arbitrary dictation.
Home Assistant Yellow uses a Raspberry Pi Compute Module, not an x86 CPU.
The old Wyoming Satellite project was archived in January 2026 and points to Linux Voice Assistant.
Linux Voice Assistant uses ESPHome and documents Linux, container and Raspberry Pi setup paths.
HAOS and Container are the supported installation types; Container has no built-in apps.
Apps were formerly add-ons; the current UI uses Settings, Apps, Install app.
Core and Supervised installation-method support ended with Home Assistant 2025.12.
Entities must be exposed to Assist before voice control; this is distinct from model installation.
Debug runs separate pipeline stages, reply URLs must be reachable, excessive gain can distort audio, and optional debug recording writes WAV files.
ATOM Echo requires its device-specific setup and firmware, not an unspecified generic satellite install.
Clear device names and room assignments help Assist resolve commands.
